name: 167. Bifrost request id survives the provider's own x-request-id (bifrost-request-id)
description:
x-bifrost-request-id is this gateway's request id on every response: the caller's x-request-id, or the UUID generated when it sent none, and the id of the request's log entry. It sits beside x-bifrost-trace-id.

The x-request-id response header is deprecated for reading that id. Provider response headers are forwarded, and OpenAI answers with its own x-request-id, which replaces the gateway's there; before x-bifrost-request-id existed, an OpenAI caller had no way to learn the id its request was logged under. Anthropic sends its request id as request-id, so x-request-id still echoes the caller's there.

Each row sends a fresh x-request-id (except the last, which sends none) and requires x-bifrost-request-id to echo it and /api/logs/{id} to find the entry: OpenAI non-streaming, streaming and the /openai drop-in, Anthropic, and OpenAI with a generated id. Run with FEATURE="bifrost-request-id".

item.name: openai gpt-4o-mini: x-bifrost-request-id echoes the caller id though OpenAI sends its own x-request-id - bifrost-request-id

exec: pm.test('x-bifrost-request-id echoes the caller request id', function () {
pm.test('the deprecated x-request-id is still present', function () {
pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('baseUrl') + '/api/logs/' + encodeURIComponent(id), method: 'GET' }, function (err, res) {
var j = null; if (!err && res.code === 200) { try { j = res.json(); } catch (e) { j = null; } }
pm.test('the log entry is found under x-bifrost-request-id', function () { pm.expect(j.id, JSON.stringify(j).slice(0, 300)).to.eql(id); });
pm.test('the log entry is found under x-bifrost-request-id', function () { pm.expect.fail('log ' + id + ' never settled: ' + (err ? String(err) : (res.code + ' ' + res.text()))); });
